questions.prompt: A researcher selects every 20th name from an alphabetically ordered register. Which sampling method is this?
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — a fixed interval through an ordered list is systematic sampling.
questions.feedbackWrong: Fixed-interval selection from a list is the definition of systematic sampling.

mistakes.misconception: Assumes any unbiased-looking selection is random.
mistakes.correction: Random sampling gives every subset equal probability — a fixed interval is deterministic once the start is chosen.

questions.prompt: X ~ B(10, 0.3). Calculate P(X = 3), giving your answer as a decimal to 3 significant figures.

A coin is tossed 20 times and shows 15 heads. A test at the 5% significance level examines whether the coin is biased towards heads. State suitable null and alternative hypotheses, and explain what the significance level means in this context.

markScheme.text: H₀: p = 0.5 (the coin is fair), where p is the probability of heads.
H₁: p > 0.5 — one-tailed because bias TOWARDS heads is claimed.
The 5% significance level is the probability of rejecting H₀ when it is actually true (a Type I error).
In context: a 5% chance of concluding the coin is biased when it is in fact fair.

mistakes.misconception: Treats the test as proof of bias or fairness.
mistakes.correction: Hypothesis tests measure evidence strength against a threshold — they never prove either hypothesis.

questions.prompt: A car accelerates uniformly from 5 m/s to 17 m/s over 8 seconds. Calculate the distance travelled in metres.
On a velocity-time graph, what does the area under the graph represent?
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — area under v–t is displacement (signed).
questions.feedbackWrong: Area under a velocity-time graph is displacement; the gradient is acceleration.

mistakes.misconception: Confuses the area with the gradient of the graph.
mistakes.correction: Gradient of v–t is acceleration; AREA is displacement — integration vs differentiation.

questions.prompt: A lift of mass 800 kg accelerates upwards at 1.5 m/s². Using Newton's second law, show how to find the tension in the cable, taking g = 9.8 m/s².

markScheme.text: Identifies forces: tension T upwards, weight 800g downwards.
Applies Newton's second law in the direction of motion: $T - 800g = 800 \times 1.5$.
$T = 9040$ N — greater than the weight because the lift accelerates upwards.

mistakes.misconception: Sets tension equal to weight — true only in equilibrium or constant velocity.
mistakes.correction: Acceleration means net force is nonzero; the tension must exceed the weight by ma.

questions.prompt: A data set has mean 40 and standard deviation 6. Every value is increased by 10, then doubled. State the new mean and standard deviation, justifying each.

markScheme.text: New mean = 100: both transformations scale/shift the mean linearly — $(40 + 10) \times 2$.
New standard deviation = 12: adding a constant does NOT change spread.
Only the doubling scales the spread — standard deviation multiplies by the scale factor (variance by its square).

mistakes.misconception: Applies the shift to the standard deviation as well as the scale.
mistakes.correction: Adding a constant moves every value together — the spread between them is unchanged.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown vertically upwards at 14 m/s. Taking g = 9.8 m/s², find the maximum height reached, in metres.
Events A and B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.5. What is P(A ∪ B)?
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — mutually exclusive events add directly: 0.3 + 0.5.
questions.feedbackWrong: Mutually exclusive means no overlap, so probabilities add: 0.8.

mistakes.misconception: Multiplies probabilities as if finding an intersection of independent events.
mistakes.correction: Multiplication finds P(A∩B) for independent events — mutually exclusive events have EMPTY intersection.

questions.prompt: A uniform plank of length 4 m rests horizontally on a pivot at its midpoint. A 30 N weight hangs 1.5 m from the pivot on the left. Explain where a 45 N weight must hang on the right for equilibrium.

markScheme.text: Equilibrium requires total clockwise moment = total anticlockwise moment about the pivot.
$d = 1$ m from the pivot on the right. The plank's own weight acts at the pivot (uniform, midpoint) so contributes no moment.
